summary:
# NOTES: "Us, and Our Charge" (Amy Le Feuvre; diary of Grisel Marjoribanks; single book)

## Cast
- **Grisel** (narrator, eldest girl, "Grizzy", "Gristle", "little mother"; mother's watch; wears mother's miniature pendant later). Keeps diary.
- **Denys**: eldest boy, "head of the family", grand manner, "Marjoribanks Major", 16+, goes to Woolwich (artillery). Wants to be soldier.
- **Aylwin**: 2nd boy, Fifth Form, argues for sport, "wiseacre", later wants Flying Corps.
- **Lynette**: 2nd girl, harum-scarum, "Scaramouche", sleepwalks/talks in sleep, hits when woken; gets "H.F." tattoo on foot.
- **Puff**: youngest, stammer, "thoughtéd", "gempleum", "Bantam", calls grandfather "Gruffy", tells tales, copies big boys.
- **Father**: Rev. Marjoribanks, Lincolnshire Rectory. Died of double pneumonia after funeral in blizzard. Last words: "Grisel—remember—tell the boys—I charge you—Hold fast! Hold fast!"
- **Mother**: Grace (née Noble). Died earlier. Defied her father to marry.
- **Aunt Mildred**: married doctor, to India. **Aunt Caroline**: died March (London).
- **Martha**: cook at Rectory. **Aylwin's donkey Andy**. **General Walton** (example grandfather).
- **Mr. Adamson**: lawyer, father's schoolfellow. **Dr. Lane**. **Mr. Scammell**: clergyman.
- **Grandfather**: Colonel Noble, Bantock Hall, near Killochan, Scotland. Gout, teeth, breakfast in bed, down ~11. Retired Army. Magistrate. Little, stout, red face, white moustache, fierce eyebrows.
- **Aunt Isobel**: Mrs. Crichton, widow, tall, grey satin, diamonds, cold, later softens. Kissed Grisel "Good little Grisel".
- **Jenkins**: butler, bald, old. **Peggy**: fat, waddling Scotch nurse; nursed mother; brushes girls' hair.
- **Ambrose**: coachman. **Slapper**: old cart horse. **Davey**: under-gardener, ex-Navy, cycles, later enlists. **Keith**: gardener. Groom (unnamed) "Slapper be a reg'lar old sheep".
- **Pat Douglas**: Irish, "Oirish", merry, "little mother", "Madam Dumps", swears ("May the de—"). Aunt **Miss Douglas** (his only relative; mother killed hunting when he was 3; father died when he was 8; lived with Irish grandparents). Cousin: captain, Royal Irish Fusiliers, Dublin.
- **Miss Garton**: governess. Tall, very beautiful, large dark eyes, fair hair, sweet smile, six brothers. Brother goes to front. Gives Grisel Isaiah 43:1 "I the LORD have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thine hand, and will keep thee."
- **Great-aunt Grisel** (Mrs. Bannock, grandfather's sister, "Aunt Grisel", "Lady Grisel", godmother). Tall, silver-grey hair, sweet, merry, "Hoots!", car, aviary of birds with names, ex-"wild" girl. Gives Grisel miniature of mother (pendant) on gold chain. Turns her house into convalescent hospital.
- **Miss Fawcett** ("Sister", Lydia Fawcett): ex-matron, tall, grey hair rolled up, big blue eyes.
- **Gervas Carrington**: older friend from Lincolnshire, Sandhurst, commissioned, gassed, lungs. Parents in India.
- **Captain Rogers**: Lincolnshire, taught Empire League; now clerk at War Office.
- **Tom Bradley**: Lincolnshire boy, wrote for 12 members.
- **Pittock**: innkeeper, Nellsolley. **David Grier**: coastguard, whisky, pipe ("David Grier" scratched on pipe). **Major Streatfield**: Chief Constable, grandfather's friend. **Mrs. Craig**: Lodge, baby. **Captain Hugh Gordon**: aeroplane pilot.
- Pets/objects: Rosebud (mother's doll, grave "IN MEMORY OF GRACE'S DARLING ROSEBUD / DESTROYED BY FLUFFIE'S PUPPIES", rose garden with yews, sunk garden). Dog "Fluffie".

## Ch I: A Bomb-shell
- Diary: a year after last entry. Aunt Mildred married, went to India. Aunt Caroline died March. Father died. Lawyer Adamson arrives.
- Denys calls council in schoolroom. Puff: "What's a minor? I thoughted they were underground coal men!"
- Adamson: grandfather (Colonel Noble) offers home to all five. Insurance £2,000 → £80–90/yr; can't touch except education.
- Mother's grandmother was Lady Louisa Noble (Denys). Grandfather "hot temper", "stiff pride". Denys: "Hem! ... Either want of brains, or want of pluck!"
- Leave Monday, one week from Tuesday. Carlisle: Adamson travels with them.
- Denys letter: "THE HEAD OF THE FAMILY" "D. MARJORIBANKS". P.S.s: Grisel ("darling mother was your daughter"), Aylwin ("rough lines on fellows of the Fifth Form"), Lynette ("General Walton"), Puff ("I hopes you have a pond with fwogs like us").
- Children imagine house: Denys (tower, rocks, sea), Aylwin (banqueting hall, rats, inventor grandfather), Lynette (garden, fountains, sunshine), Grisel (cold stern town house with parade), Puff (big hall; "God lives everywhere"; "Not in wicked people's houses. The devil lives with them.").
- Grisel: "we can't get away from God." Denys: "crisis in our lives."

## Ch II: Our New Home
- Last Sunday at Rectory. Farewell visits. Mr. Scammell.
- Father's seat talk: verses found: "Hold fast that which is good" (chosen as their charge); "Hold fast the form of sound words"; "That which ye have already hold fast till I come"; "Hold that fast which thou hast, that no man take thy crown." Lynette: "Grisel... if I hold fast to what I have already, it will be badness." Denys: "we must get the thing first."
- Journey: Glasgow 7pm; Killochan station; stationmaster ("the Kornel have sent the carriage"). Brougham. Boys sit outside/inside.
- Hall: butler: "They're at dinner, sir." Aunt Isobel (pale grey satin, diamonds). Kisses Puff. Peggy: "Ye'll be Miss Grace's bairns, and I nursed her."
- Nursery wing behind green baize door. Boys' room: three beds. Lynette and Grisel share room (mother's old room).
- Morning: sea view. Prayer; "Daily Light". Sea adventure; forgot breakfast; Peggy fetches them. Peggy: "Miss Grisel's ... ring a big bell". Aunt Isobel: "We have no prayers."
- Grandfather summons: "Miss Grace's family, sir!"

## Ch III: We Explore
- Library: grandfather "I say! What a crowd of them!" Denys's speech; grandfather: "I wash my hands of 'em all." Denys: "We're Empire-builders"; grandfather: "Young Jackanapes!" Isobel: "pack them off to the school". Puff: "I never has had a nursery... I won't be putted in it."
- Isobel: boys to school ~20 miles; governess in 3 weeks; "We have no prayers. If we want you, we shall send for you." Pocket money: Aylwin: "stony broke", Grisel has 2½d.
- Denys drives cart with Slapper; Ambrose: "Very well, sir."
- Rose garden: Grisel finds Rosebud grave; prays "Hold fast".
- Puff nearly falls into pond. Dinner: hot leg of mutton, jam roly-poly.
- Groom: "Slapper be a reg'lar old sheep!" Lynette's hat tied on Slapper. Cliff cry "Hi! Help!"

## Ch IV: A Rescue
- Boy hanging on cliff. Reins tied; chain of pulling; Grisel prays "O God, make us very strong!"
- Pat Douglas: merry, curls, "I thought I was a goner!" "Have you descended from the skies?"
- Slapper gone; tracked wheel marks; Pat joins.
- Pat's background: Irish; stocks; "run in for assault". Lives with aunt 15 miles away. Pat's sail-boat.
- Nellsolley: Pittock's inn. Denys wants tip; Grisel refuses borrowing ("Father always made us promise never to borrow"; "Hold fast!").
- Pat kisses reins; "for saving my worthless life."
- Grandfather: "Pat Douglas!... a thorough bad lot... My new reins were worth more than he was." Gives 2-shilling piece. Forbids Pat's boat.
- Peggy tells Pat's history (mother killed, father died, "terrible laddie", nine lives).
- Puff alone with grandfather: "Hullo, old gempleum!" Calls him "Gruffy", given ring, fox-hunt promise, pony promise.

## Ch V: Missing
- Morning; Davey takes boat out; Pat's sailing boat found drifting, empty; Davey: "Where he be now is past me!" Four islands.
- Aunt Isobel (in rose garden): "Your mother and I used to sit here... You are very like her." Grisel tells "Hold fast" charge; Isobel: "Life is hard on one's memories!" "Good little Grisel!"
- Grandfather: "if you had had your wish, you would have been all at the bottom of the sea with him."
- Night: Denys wakes Grisel: light on island, going to Davey's cottage; Lynette sleep-talks; prayer.
- Morning: boys gone; Peggy: "Dearie me, what feckless wicked laddies!" Grandfather's boat missing.
- Grisel & Lynette row with Davey to island; grandfather's boat in cove; cave; Denys's head at hole.

## Ch VI: A Long Sunday
- Aylwin head: "Pat is with you". Davey: "he'll always turn up again, will that limb of a boy!"
- Pat's story: left basket on island; boat drifted; cut leg; hid in cave; fire; tide trapped boys; Denys and Aylwin rescued in morning.
- Miss Douglas on horse: "Oh Pat, you'll be my death one day."
- Doctor sews Pat's leg. Pat stays a few days. Ghost stories.
- Pat: "rescued two days running... so as to be quits!"
- Lynette: Pat says "Oh Lord!", "May the devil take me" (swearing).
- Sunday wet; no church. Pat's cards; Grisel: "Hold fast!" leaves room. Puff's cushions.
- Denys reads lessons; hymns; Pat sings beautifully. "next time I hope I shall be the one to call out 'Hold fast.'"
- Afternoon: cliffs walk; visitors; motor. Empire talk; Pat: "I'll enlist as a drummer-boy" "I'll marry Grisel"-type joking.
- Ends: "awful row... Aunt Isobel is furious."

## Ch VII: Pat Leaves Us
- Puff runs through baize door; gallery slide down banister (Pat's idea). Jenkins falls with tray of glasses. Lynette grabbed his legs. Grandfather swears. Visitors present.
- Isobel: "I did think, Grisel, that you were a good little girl... I am bitterly disappointed in you." Cut glass worth £20; Jenkins bruise. Governess summoned by telegram.
- Pat: "Cheer up, Madam Dumps!" Plates joke: "St. Patrick and St. Grisel".
- Isobel interview: Grisel: "stretched out too long... goes snap." Boys in schoolroom; Isobel: Pat going home.
- Puff's "thumb cut" = paint on handkerchief; boys trick Peggy; Pat locks Grisel and Lynette out, pockets key. Grisel: "Oh, you can do anything if you tell lies." Pat: "Do you call meself a liar?"
- Lie debate at lunch; Pat's "slay me" knife joke.
- Pat leaves with Miss Douglas: "give me a grand licking with your tongue." Grisel: "I hate you when you speak like that!"
- Schoolroom cleaning: dead mouse, paste basin spilled; Isobel and Miss Garton arrive.

## Ch VIII: Our Governess
- Miss Garton: beautiful, dark eyes, fair hair; "Are we going to be friends, Grisel?" Had six brothers.
- Denys & Aylwin: tea; Puff kicked under table; Aylwin apologises. Puff: "shall have my tea with grandfather."
- Grisel mends Puff's stockings; complains: "We're all treated as if we are troublesome."
- Miss Garton: "Puff ... too many managing him"; "rather hard upon him." Puff tells grandfather: no seeing them till summer.
- Denys: "H.F." reminder; "All serene! ... I shall remember 'H.F.'"; Denys & Aylwin visit fishermen's cottages.
- Boys leave (packing). Grandfather gives each boy a sovereign ("took our pills, and then had the jam").
- Tattoos: Denys & Aylwin "H.F." on left wrist (old sailor). Aylwin: "Happy Fellow"; Lynette: "Happy Fool". Miss Garton: "Let the letters sink into your hearts."
- Lynette gets "H.F." on foot; Grisel wants one too (forbidden). Lynette "rose" joke.
- Sunday walk: Miss Garton shows Isaiah 43:1 verse; "Hold fast to His Hand." Grisel prays to take God's hand.
- Lynette: "I'm not sure I want to be [good]."

## Ch IX: My Godmother
- Lunch 1pm; Puff goes to grandfather. Lynette hides in study cupboard to eavesdrop on Puff. Puff's speech: "I'll go up to Jesus Christ... inside the moon?"; grandfather: Denys to inherit.
- Cupboard jammed; bottle falls; Lynette bursts out; grandfather shakes her; Lynette: "wicked old man". Teeth in hand. Lynette: "I was very rude."
- Lynette: "I don't feel that God cares about me a bit." Grisel: "Father loved me."—Lynette apologises; grandfather forgives. Father's maxim: "Confession to God and frank apology to man blots out a sin."
- Aunt Isobel: godmother Aunt Grisel (Mrs. Bannock) invites Grisel. Car, 10 miles. Turret house with church windows. Aunt Grisel: "She's her mother over again!"; "You have her eyes and mouth, and a bit of her soul."
- Story: mother at five, sat in corner; "First I was a little imp... then sweet little angel... Aunt Grisel's and God's little angel."
- Tea: silver cake-basket with cupids. Invitation: next Saturday week, car, Lynette too.

## Ch X: The Beginning of War
- Peggy on Aunt Grisel: wild; Mr. Dick (died India); Mr. Bannock (her husband) wedding story "my last day of liberty".
- Aunt Grisel visit: aviary with birds named; gives miniature (mother, pearls, blue velvet band) on gold chain. "If the want is there, the rest will follow!"
- Lynette: "She is saying 'Hold fast!'"
- Pat: Home Rule Bill, Ulster; wants to fight.
- War declared (grandfather at front door: "England has declared war against Germany!"). Denys: "God save the King!" Denys wants to enlist.
- Empire League song "Land of our Birth" (verses quoted). Pledge "Head, heart, and hand through the years to be."
- Denys writes League letter ("HOLD FAST TO YOUR PLEDGE"; "DEAR MEMBER AND COMRADE"). 12 letters sent with roll-call names; shilling of stamps.

## Ch XI: The First Recruit
- Pat: wants Irish regiment; aunt says no; cousin captain Royal Irish Fusiliers.
- Grandfather asks Denys to fetch paper; drives to town; Denys/Aylwin/Pat ride; Pat enlists at town hall (Irish Rifles). Pat's horse jumps gate; arm sprained; sling; transferred to cousin's regiment in Ireland.
- Pat's leaving: "I'll marry Grisel, if she'll have me!" Boys laugh; Pat: "She'd drag me through Heaven's Gate."
- Grisel gives father's little Testament; writes verse "I the LORD have called thee..." in it. Pat: "Testaments always stop bullets."
- Debate about war, sport and pheasant killing; Denys: "Girls are too small-minded."
- Tom Bradley letter: nine of twelve enlisting. Denys credited.
- Gervas got commission; Denys "born two years too late".

## Ch XII: Aunt Grisel's Hospital
- Denys to Woolwich (grandfather got him included). "I'm going to be in the artillery."
- Isobel: "Denys is too young... no constitution." Grandfather: "I'll give 'em a rounding up myself" (lecture on war).
- Grisel recites pledge to grandfather. Grandfather: "Germans are making short work of women in Belgium."
- Denys's last night: Grisel writes Isaiah verse in his Bible; "Semper fidelis! Semper paratus!" "H.F."
- Aunt Grisel's house converted to hospital; Grisel plans wards; "Dream away, child." Letter from Aunt Grisel: "MY DEAR, ROMANTIC GODDAUGHTER"; War Office accepted offer; Miss Fawcett (Lydia) running it.
- Grandfather: Miss Fawcett "very handsome woman", ex-matron.

## Ch XIII: Our Search
- Hospital work: bandages, scrap-books; Miss Fawcett: "Don't hurry to grow up." Lynette: nerves vs. wounded.
- Spies talk; David Grier (coastguard, whisky).
- Monday: Miss Garton away (brother to front). Lynette & Grisel row to island with Denys's torch, rope, matches; stable lads push boat.
- Cave: smell of tobacco; pipe (Lynette pockets); rotten boards; barrel; oil tins (motor-oil smell). Cough; man with pipe. Hide; escape.

## Ch XIV: The Find
- Burly man (seaboots, blue jersey, knitted cap, Scots dialect). Holds them. "I'll come an' murder ye in yer beds." They swear silence.
- Rowing home; thank God on beach; Lynette: "I suppose he wasn't painting a boat!"
- Grandfather: "Bosh!"; telephone to Major Streatfield. Grandfather laughs.
- Next morning: captured oil; no man. Pipe = David Grier's. Found light with slow-burning fuse in cave cleft. Major: "great courage and presence of mind."
- Lynette tries to take armour shield; grandfather refuses.
- Local paper note on Chief Constable. David Grier removed; replaced.

## Ch XV: An Old Friend
- Grisel arranges flowers; wounded: gassed (Gervas Carrington), head-wound paralysis, deaf-mute, nerves.
- Gervas: "I thought there weren't many Grisels in the world." "Little Grisel!... I would rather see you than any one else... next to my mother."
- Grisel tells Gervas everything; Miss Fawcett = "Sister".
- Gervas: "You're growing up." "She always inspires!"
- Lynette wants V.C.
- Pat's letter (censor's ticket): "DEAR LITTLE MOTHER GRISEL"; trenches; major "McAndrew"; general's remark; "How is the Puffer! My love to the Scaramouche." Signed "Your worthless PAT."
- Christmas holidays; Aylwin home; Denys home soon. Captain Hugh Gordon's aeroplane; flight with Aylwin; Puff: "find heaven when you're up there."
- Aylwin: Flying Corps. Lynette: marry a V.C. Grisel: "women are at great disadvantage"; wants to die like mother.

## Ch XVI: Sad News
- New Year's Eve: Gervas to tea; dinner downstairs; "Auld Lang Syne" on terrace. Gervas: "Second Coming... King comes into His own."
- Pat's commission in another Irish regiment; Miss Douglas: "my wild laddie is going to do something yet."
- Denys to France (after Woolwich; ~6-month course).
- Easter: storm. Aunt Isobel: "He was killed yesterday." Pat killed. Puff: "he's gone just like father."
- Lynette: "Why doesn't God strike the Kaiser dead?" Grisel: prays for Pat twice daily.
- Miss Douglas visit: colonel's letter (storming trench; Pat rallied men; hit when trench taken). Pat's last words: "Rather dull work for you fellows—ever so much obliged to you. You've carried me A1." Nurse's message: "Tell Grisel—first leaf in Testament—made good to me. And I've found the Hand to H.F. to." Pat died after four hours.
- Testament returned to Grisel (stained); Grisel keeps it and letter in "treasure box".
- Denys leaves for France (24 hrs leave). "if I share Pat's fate... Aylwin takes my place." Denys gripping left wrist with right: keep father's Charge.

**FINIS**
